chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The woad loosened my molars.'

key_terms.الْوَسَمَةُ: Woad, a plant used for dyeing, specifically noted here for its effect on teeth.

ai.seo_question: What is the effect of woad (wasamah) on the teeth according to Imam Abu Ja'far?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) notes that the dyeing plant *wasamah* (woad) had the specific effect of loosening his molars, a detail often cited in discussions regarding the physical properties and permissibility of natural dyes. This narration highlights the practical observations of the Imams regarding medicinal or cosmetic substances, linking physical effects to broader rulings on purity and adornment in Shia jurisprudence. It serves as a foundational text in *al-Kafi* for understanding the characteristics of black dye derived from woad versus other sources.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal Bin Maymoun, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> molar was loosened by the woad (a dyeing plant)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “
Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Woad has affected my molar teeth. 5 ”
